cells.tense: The person is here at the desk with the pen, and the light is doing what it does.
cells.ask: Pick one direction you've been steering by and haven't said out loud, and say it plainly to one person this week.
cells.core:
The light arrived. It wasn't invented and it wasn't summoned. You looked up one day and there was a direction, and you followed it until following stopped being effort. Whatever grew out of that has grown in and isn't asking anything of you now except to be seen. Not straining to shine, not managing the glow, just standing where the work has already carried you and letting it land on whoever's nearby. You can hold a lot. Holding and shining pull the same way, and that happens less often than either one alone.

There's more light when you look around than you can compare it to. So test it small. Say one thing about where you're actually pointed, and let someone hear it without working to agree. The shine doesn't need defending and doesn't need translating. It needs one witness who isn't you.
cells.sheetLine: You looked up and found your direction and let it be seen.
cells.verb: orienting by a light one did not set
cells.place: under the weight of the form that has to keep holding

cells.tense: You are already standing in a future where the light has landed, and you are bracing inside it.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're anticipating as if it's already yours, and don't act on it for one day.
cells.core:
The light has stopped being a direction and become a searchlight pointed forward. Everything gets lit ahead of time — the room you'll be in, the people who'll finally see it, the version of this that arrives whole — and you're holding your body ready for a morning that hasn't come. That's a kind of endurance, keeping vigil for a dawn that can't be scheduled. But the light you're proposing is dazzling the people who'd otherwise be lit by it. They can't see what you're showing them because it's already too bright and too far ahead.

The brilliance is real. The timing has run ahead of what's actually here. Direct knowing doesn't need to be proven in advance — it lands or it doesn't, and it'll land when it lands. Pick one thing you're living toward like it's settled, and let it sit unsettled with you for a full day. No arranging. No brightening it for anyone. Hold it unlit and see what stays true.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that has already closed behind you, and the light that used to guide is back there.
cells.ask: Do one small kind thing for something already growing in your life, and notice it without asking it to become more.
cells.core:
The cultivation happened and the flowering didn't. That's the shape of it. You kept going long after the light that started it stopped being visible, and you did it on endurance alone, and endurance is what's left. You are still holding. The weight is still being carried. But the light under the load has gone quiet, and the shine that used to be automatic is now something you remember other people having.

Don't push at the place that's empty. Water a plant you already have. Sit with a person who doesn't need you to be bright. Tend something that's already growing and let it grow at its own pace. Care given to something smaller comes back through whatever has run dry. It doesn't come by straining. It comes by caring and letting that be enough on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You kept going past the light and now tend something small.

cells.tense: You are writing in the room already, and the pen is down, and you do not know the writing is yours.
cells.ask: Catch one moment today when someone is steadied by being near you, and say to yourself that this is something you are carrying.
cells.core:
The shining is running and the account of it is somewhere else. People stand near you and things get held. They bring you weight you don't notice taking. The light you carry is doing what it does whether you're watching it or not, and the story you tell about that is that it's just the situation, just the people, just how it goes. You describe yourself as holding on, and you are. You are also the thing being held onto, and that hasn't occurred to you.

This is a quiet misattribution, not a failure. You've just stopped noticing your own hand in it. Start with one moment — someone steadier because you were in the room, or calmer because you didn't flinch. Stand still for it and say, to yourself, this is mine carrying that. Not a report to anyone. A correction to your own ledger.
cells.sheetLine: Something's being carried here and you're the one carrying it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim in my draft is that any given person in this seat has a fully-grown, finished cultiv ation driving their visible brightness; the record supports only the mechanism, not their history or motives. A reader could reasonably say they're shining from recent effort, borrowed light, or habit rather than completion. The ask survives being wrong because it is small and concrete in both cases. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line implying I know what they've cultivated underneath.
